item.content:encoded:
The SpaceX Intern Program offers university students and graduate students the opportunity to gain hands-on experience while contributing to real projects in the aerospace and space technology industry. The year-round program provides opportunities across a wide range of engineering functions, software roles, and business operations, allowing interns to work alongside SpaceX employees on challenging projects.

Unlike a traditional internship focused primarily on observation or classroom-style learning, SpaceX states that interns can receive substantial responsibility and play an important role in the company’s work. Successful applicants typically demonstrate both strong academic performance and meaningful hands-on experience through extracurricular projects, university teams, previous employment, internships, or similar activities.

About the SpaceX Intern Program

SpaceX describes its internship program as an opportunity for students to contribute directly to the company’s work in space exploration and its broader goal of making humanity a multiplanetary species.

Interns can work across both technical and non-technical areas of the company. Depending on the specific position, responsibilities may involve designing, developing, testing, manufacturing, analyzing, researching, coordinating, or supporting business operations.

The program is designed to provide students with practical experience that complements their university education.

SpaceX emphasizes that interns are not simply observers. Interns can be given significant responsibilities and may contribute to projects alongside full-time employees.

SpaceX Internship Opportunities

SpaceX offers internship opportunities across multiple areas of the organization.

1. Engineering

Engineering interns can participate in work involving the development of spaceflight hardware and related systems.

Engineering internship responsibilities may include areas such as:

  • Design
  • Development
  • Testing
  • Manufacturing
  • Engineering analysis
  • Hardware development
  • Hands-on technical projects

The exact responsibilities depend on the specific engineering position and team.

2. Software

Software internships are also available within the program.

Students interested in software may have the opportunity to contribute to projects involving software development and other technical challenges associated with SpaceX operations.

SpaceX notes that software internship applicants may include students enrolled in graduate programs by the beginning of employment.

3. Business Operations

The program is not limited to engineering and software.

SpaceX also offers opportunities in business operations, where interns contribute to the company’s broader business objectives.

These roles demonstrate that students from non-engineering disciplines can also find opportunities within the SpaceX Intern Program when they possess relevant skills and experience.

Difference Between a SpaceX Intern and Graduate Engineer

SpaceX distinguishes between its internship positions and graduate engineer positions.

Internships

Internships are available to technical and non-technical candidates who are currently enrolled at a four-year accredited university.

For business operations and software roles, candidates may also be enrolled in a graduate program by the beginning of employment.

Interns can contribute to actual company projects and gain hands-on professional experience.

Graduate Engineer Positions

Graduate engineer positions are specifically intended for engineering graduates.

Candidates must have:

  • Completed a bachelor’s degree in engineering, physics, or mathematics; and
  • Be enrolled in a graduate program by the beginning of employment.

Graduate engineers work on actual space hardware development projects and are expected to work both independently and collaboratively.

What Does SpaceX Look For in Intern Candidates?

According to SpaceX, strong candidates typically have more than good academic results.

The company highlights two important areas:

  1. Strong academic performance
  2. Significant hands-on extracurricular project experience

This means students can strengthen their applications by demonstrating that they have actually applied what they have learned.

For example, relevant experience could include:

  • University engineering projects
  • Student-led technical organizations
  • Coding projects
  • Design and manufacturing projects
  • Research projects
  • Business or entrepreneurial projects
  • Team-based university initiatives
  • Previous internships
  • Relevant employment
  • Other practical projects connected to the position

SpaceX states that successful candidates for advanced internships and entry-level full-time positions often participate in student-driven projects involving designing, building, testing, or coding.

For non-technical internship candidates, SpaceX looks for comparable hands-on project experience relevant to their particular field.

When Are SpaceX Internships Available?

One of the notable features of the SpaceX Intern Program is that opportunities are available year-round.

Interns and graduate engineers must be available to work full time for a minimum of 12 weeks.

The program operates across three main seasons:

Spring

January – April

Summer

May – August

Fall

September – December

Students should therefore monitor SpaceX’s careers website regularly because opportunities can be posted for different locations and seasons.

SpaceX Internship Locations

SpaceX lists internship and graduate engineer opportunities across multiple locations in the United States.

Locations listed in the program information include:

  • Bastrop, Texas
  • Cape Canaveral, Florida
  • Hawthorne, California
  • Irvine, California
  • McGregor, Texas
  • Redmond, Washington
  • Starbase, Texas
  • Sunnyvale, California
  • Vandenberg, California
  • Washington, DC
  • Bloomfield, Connecticut
  • Long Beach, California
  • Woodinville, Washington

SpaceX notes that site availability varies by season, meaning not every location will necessarily have internship positions available during every internship period.

Applicants should therefore check the individual internship listing for the location and term associated with each position.

Can Master’s and PhD Students Apply?

Yes.

SpaceX states that its Intern Program demographics are predominantly made up of upperclassmen and graduate students.

Students pursuing master’s or PhD-level education may therefore be eligible for appropriate internship opportunities.

Students enrolled in engineering graduate programs may also qualify for graduate engineer positions, provided they meet the specific educational requirements.

The precise eligibility requirements can vary depending on the position, so applicants should carefully review each individual job posting.

Does SpaceX Recruit Only From Certain Universities?

No.

SpaceX states that there is no single set of universities or colleges from which it exclusively recruits.

Instead, the company emphasizes the importance of what candidates have actually accomplished.

For technical applicants, this can include participation in student-driven engineering groups where students design, build, test, or code projects.

For non-technical applicants, comparable hands-on project experience in their respective fields can also be valuable.

This means that attending a particular university is not presented as a requirement for applying to the program.

Are International Students Eligible?

International applicants face specific restrictions because SpaceX works with technologies subject to U.S. government export regulations.

SpaceX states that, to comply with International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and other U.S. government space technology export regulations, applicants must fall into one of the following categories:

  • U.S. citizens
  • Lawful permanent residents of the United States
  • Protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)
  • Individuals who are eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State

Therefore, being a university student outside the United States does not by itself establish eligibility.

International applicants must meet the applicable authorization requirements for the particular position.

Can F-1 Visa Students Receive Sponsorship?

SpaceX specifically states that it cannot provide employment sponsorship to students holding F-1 visa status.

Students currently studying in the United States under F-1 status should therefore take this restriction into account when assessing their eligibility.

Because immigration and export-control requirements can be position-specific, applicants should also review the requirements stated in the individual internship posting.

Is There a Minimum GPA Requirement?

There is no minimum GPA requirement for the SpaceX Intern Program.

However, SpaceX states that it has a preferred cumulative GPA of 3.5 or higher.

This means that a GPA below 3.5 does not automatically prevent someone from applying according to the information provided, although academic performance remains part of the overall candidate profile.

Applicants should also focus on demonstrating relevant projects, technical or professional experience, and their individual contributions to previous work.

What Should You Include on Your SpaceX Internship Resume?

SpaceX recommends that applicants provide specific information on their resumes.

1. University Information

Include:

  • University name
  • Degree
  • Major or majors
  • Cumulative GPA
  • Expected graduation date

2. Previous Experience

Include relevant:

  • Internships
  • Co-ops
  • Jobs
  • Other professional experience

Experience should be relevant to the particular internship wherever possible.

3. Project Experience

SpaceX particularly encourages applicants to describe relevant project-team involvement.

Your resume should communicate:

  • The project you worked on
  • Your role
  • What you personally contributed
  • The challenges you encountered
  • What you accomplished

Simply listing a project may not fully demonstrate your abilities. Applicants should make their individual contribution clear.

SpaceX Internship Interview Process

Candidates who are selected for interviews may go through several stages.

SpaceX states that candidates may undergo technical phone screens.

Depending on the specific team and position, candidates may also be required to complete:

  • A quiz
  • A project
  • A programming test
  • Other technical assessments

The interview process can therefore vary depending on the position.

APPLY HERE

How Should Applicants Prepare for the Interview?

SpaceX recommends that candidates be prepared to discuss their most significant technical achievements.

Applicants should be able to explain:

  • What project they worked on
  • What problem they were trying to solve
  • What their individual contribution was
  • What challenges they encountered
  • How they approached those challenges
  • How they innovated
  • How they improved or advanced the project
  • What they learned from the experience

A particularly important point is being able to distinguish your contribution from the work completed by the broader team.

For example, rather than simply saying that you were part of a project, you should be prepared to explain exactly what you designed, developed, tested, researched, analyzed, organized, or improved.

SpaceX also recommends that candidates understand the company’s mission and be able to explain how that mission relates to their own skills.

How Long Does the Recruitment Process Take?

Applicants should be prepared for the recruitment process to take some time.

SpaceX states that it receives a large volume of applications and cannot personally respond to every applicant.

Recruiters will contact candidates who are selected for interviews.

SpaceX also notes that recruiting for a particular internship or graduate engineer position can take up to six months.

Applicants should therefore not necessarily interpret a lack of immediate communication as a final decision.

Should You Reapply If You Are Not Selected?

Yes.

SpaceX encourages applicants who are not selected to continue applying for future opportunities.

Because there are many applicants and a limited number of internship and graduate engineer positions, applicants may want to continue monitoring the careers page.

SpaceX also recommends applying to multiple locations and internship terms to increase visibility and opportunities for consideration.

However, each application should still be relevant to the applicant’s qualifications and interests.

Are SpaceX Internships Paid?

Yes.

SpaceX states that its internships and graduate engineer opportunities are paid.

This makes the program different from unpaid internships where students may receive professional experience without financial compensation.

The supplied program information does not state a specific internship salary or hourly rate, so applicants should check the individual job posting for compensation details where available.

Can SpaceX Internships Count Toward University Course Credit?

Yes, potentially.

SpaceX states that internships and graduate engineer positions can be used to satisfy course credit at the discretion of the student’s university.

This means the decision ultimately depends on the student’s institution and its academic requirements.

Students who need an internship for academic credit should therefore consult their university or academic department before assuming that the SpaceX position will automatically satisfy their requirements.

Restrictions on Internship Work and Academic Reports

Because SpaceX interns may work with proprietary, sensitive, and/or ITAR-controlled projects, there are restrictions on publicly presenting internship work.

SpaceX states that it cannot allow interns to create presentations, papers, or reports about the work they complete at the company when the work involves these protected areas.

Where necessary, SpaceX can confirm the dates of employment to a university or instructor and provide a brief overview of the type of experience provided through the internship.

Students who need to submit a detailed internship report as part of their academic program should therefore consider this restriction before accepting a position and discuss the requirements with their university.

SpaceX Intern Program: Key Details

Detail Information
Opportunity SpaceX Intern Program
Organization SpaceX
Opportunity type Paid internship / graduate engineer opportunities
Fields Engineering, software, business operations and related functions
Availability Year-round
Duration Minimum 12 weeks, full time
Seasons Spring, Summer, Fall
Locations Multiple locations across the United States
Graduate students Eligible for applicable internship opportunities
GPA No minimum; 3.5+ preferred
International applicants Subject to U.S. export-control/ITAR eligibility
F-1 sponsorship Not provided
Course credit Possible, subject to university discretion
Deadline No single program-wide deadline stated
Application Through individual SpaceX internship job postings

Application Process

SpaceX does not provide one universal application deadline for the entire Intern Program.

Instead, applicants should search the company’s careers website for currently available internship positions and apply to positions that match their qualifications, field, preferred location, and available season.

Because opportunities are posted throughout the year, students should monitor the internship listings regularly.

Apply for current SpaceX internship opportunities:

View SpaceX Internships

Important Eligibility Considerations for International Applicants

For students applying from outside the United States, eligibility is particularly important.

The program information does not state that all international students are eligible simply because they meet the academic requirements.

Instead, SpaceX states that applicants must satisfy applicable U.S. government space technology export regulations, including ITAR requirements.

Therefore, applicants from countries outside the United States should carefully review the eligibility requirements of each individual position and determine whether they can obtain the necessary authorization.

The supplied information does not provide a list of specific countries whose citizens are automatically eligible.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is primarily aimed at students currently enrolled in higher education, including:

  • Undergraduate students at four-year accredited universities
  • Upperclassmen
  • Graduate students
  • Master’s students
  • PhD students, where applicable
  • Engineering students who meet graduate engineer requirements
  • Students pursuing technical disciplines
  • Students pursuing non-technical disciplines relevant to business operations
  • Students with relevant hands-on project experience

Academic Requirements

For standard internships:

  • Candidates should be currently enrolled at a four-year accredited university.
  • Business operations and software applicants may also be enrolled in a graduate program by the start of employment.

For graduate engineer positions:

  • Candidates must have completed a bachelor’s degree in engineering, physics, or mathematics.
  • They must be enrolled in a graduate program by the beginning of employment.

There is no stated minimum GPA, although a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or higher is preferred.

Nationality and Geographic Eligibility

SpaceX states that applicants must satisfy applicable U.S. government export-control requirements.

Eligible individuals must be one of the following:

  • U.S. citizen
  • U.S. lawful permanent resident
  • Protected individual under the specified U.S. law
  • An individual eligible to obtain the necessary U.S. Department of State authorization

The supplied information does not identify a specific list of African, European, Asian, or other countries whose nationals can automatically apply.

For applicants from countries such as Zambia, eligibility should therefore be determined based on the applicable authorization requirements rather than assuming that nationality alone qualifies or disqualifies an applicant.

Visit HERE to learn more the SpaceX Intern Program 2026

Deadline

No single program-wide deadline is stated.

SpaceX operates its internship program throughout the year, with Spring, Summer, and Fall opportunities. Individual internship positions may have their own application timelines, so applicants should check the specific job listing for the position and term they are interested in.

Conclusion

The SpaceX Intern Program provides university and graduate students with an opportunity to gain paid, full-time, hands-on experience in one of the world’s major space technology companies. Opportunities span engineering, software, business operations, and other functions, meaning the program is not limited exclusively to engineering students.

SpaceX places considerable emphasis on practical experience, academic performance, and evidence that applicants have actively contributed to projects. Students should therefore look beyond their GPA and build a strong record of relevant projects, extracurricular activities, internships, employment, research, coding, design, or other hands-on work.

The program is available across multiple U.S. locations and operates during Spring, Summer, and Fall seasons, with a minimum commitment of 12 weeks. Internships are paid and may potentially count toward university course credit.

For international students, however, U.S. export-control and ITAR requirements are a major eligibility consideration, and SpaceX does not provide employment sponsorship for students on F-1 visas. Applicants should carefully examine the eligibility requirements attached to each individual position before applying.

Students interested in pursuing an internship should regularly monitor the SpaceX careers page because opportunities are available throughout the year and individual positions may have different requirements and timelines.

item.content:encoded:
The Lynette A. Turner Pathways to Consulting Fellowship, offered by AMS Planning & Research, is an opportunity designed to increase the participation of people from historically underrepresented groups in the arts and culture consulting field. The fellowship provides practical professional training, mentorship, and exposure to consulting work involving arts organizations, cultural institutions, and the wider arts and culture sector.

The programme was established to help nurture future leaders and foster greater inclusiveness within arts and culture consulting. Through project-based experience and engagement with experienced professionals, fellows can develop skills in research, planning, quantitative analysis, writing, and industry research.

The fellowship may be undertaken either in person or remotely, giving participants the opportunity to engage with AMS Planning & Research through different working arrangements.

About AMS Planning & Research

AMS Planning & Research is a consulting firm working in the arts, culture, and entertainment sectors. Its work involves supporting arts organizations and cultural institutions through planning, research, analysis, and related consulting services.

The firm’s professional experience provides fellows with exposure to the kinds of challenges and projects encountered by organizations operating in the arts and culture sector. By participating in the fellowship, individuals can gain insight into how consulting supports organizational planning, decision-making, and the development of arts and cultural institutions.

The fellowship is also connected to AMS’s commitment to expanding participation in a field where some communities have historically been underrepresented.

About the Lynette A. Turner Pathways to Consulting Fellowship

The Lynette A. Turner Pathways to Consulting Fellowship was created to support and increase the involvement of individuals from Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC) populations in arts and culture consulting.

The programme was initiated in 2020 and, according to AMS Planning & Research, has engaged 13 fellows since its inception. Its purpose is to help participants gain practical experience, develop professional skills, and explore opportunities for leadership within the discipline.

Rather than focusing exclusively on theoretical learning, the fellowship involves practical work connected to real consulting projects. Fellows have opportunities to contribute to research and planning activities, work alongside experienced professionals, and engage in training and dialogue.

The programme is intended to help strengthen inclusiveness within arts and culture consulting while supporting the professional development of individuals from communities that have been underrepresented in the field.

Fellowship Format: In-Person or Remote Participation

The fellowship offers flexibility in how participants engage with the programme. It may be completed either in person or remotely.

This arrangement may allow participants to take part without necessarily needing to relocate, depending on the specific expectations and arrangements of the fellowship.

Regardless of the format, fellows are expected to engage with the programme’s professional activities, including practical project work, training, mentorship, and discussions with AMS staff.

Applicants should consult the official fellowship position for details about the available working arrangements, participation expectations, and any location-related requirements.

Practical Training and Responsibilities

A central component of the Lynette A. Turner Pathways to Consulting Fellowship is the opportunity to contribute to consulting work. Fellows may support a range of projects involving small organizations and major arts and cultural institutions.

The responsibilities described by AMS Planning & Research include the following.

1. Project Planning and Research

Fellows may assist with project planning and research efforts for organizations across the arts and culture sector.

This work can provide exposure to how consulting projects are organized, how information is gathered, and how research contributes to planning and decision-making. Participants may gain an understanding of the needs of different organizations and how consultants help address those needs.

Working on projects involving both small organizations and major cultural institutions may also expose fellows to a variety of organizational contexts and challenges.

2. Quantitative Analysis

The fellowship includes opportunities to support quantitative analysis.

Quantitative analysis involves working with numerical information to identify patterns, examine trends, and support conclusions. In a consulting context, this can help organizations understand their operations, audiences, markets, or other areas relevant to a project.

By assisting with this work, fellows can gain practical exposure to the use of data and analytical methods in professional consulting.

The source does not specify particular software, statistical methods, or technical qualifications required for this responsibility. Applicants should refer to the official position description for further details.

3. Research and Writing

Fellows may assist with research and writing activities connected to consulting projects.

These responsibilities can involve gathering and reviewing information, organizing findings, and helping communicate research in a clear and useful format. Research and writing are important parts of consulting because recommendations and project decisions often depend on reliable information and well-presented findings.

The experience may help participants strengthen their research, analytical thinking, and professional writing skills.

4. Industry and Consumer Research

Another responsibility is conducting industry and consumer research.

This work can help organizations understand the broader environment in which they operate, including industry developments and the needs or interests of consumers and audiences.

For arts and cultural institutions, research of this kind can contribute to understanding audiences, identifying trends, and informing planning decisions.

Through this work, fellows can gain exposure to how research is used to support organizations in the arts, culture, and entertainment sectors.

APPLY HERE

Mentorship from Experienced Sector Leaders

The fellowship provides participants with mentorship from recognized leaders in the sector.

Mentorship can help fellows learn from professionals who have experience working in arts and culture consulting. It can also provide opportunities to ask questions, gain insight into professional practice, and better understand the skills and approaches required in the field.

In addition to mentorship, participants engage in training and dialogue with AMS Planning & Research staff. The organization describes its staff as collectively bringing decades of expertise in the arts and culture arena.

This combination of practical work, training, and professional engagement is intended to help fellows build their understanding of the consulting field and develop skills that can support their future careers.

Professional Development and Career Exposure

The Lynette A. Turner Pathways to Consulting Fellowship is designed to help participants develop professionally while gaining direct exposure to arts and culture consulting.

Through their involvement in projects, fellows can gain experience in areas such as:

  • Project planning and research

  • Quantitative analysis

  • Research and professional writing

  • Industry and consumer research

  • Collaboration with experienced professionals

  • Understanding the work of arts and cultural institutions

The fellowship may also help participants become more familiar with the consulting profession and the range of work carried out within the arts and culture sector.

AMS Planning & Research notes that experience at the organization may provide fellows with a competitive advantage when seeking employment in the arts and culture sector. This should be understood as a potential benefit of the experience, rather than a guarantee of employment or a future position.

Who Is the Fellowship Designed For?

The programme is specifically designed to engage members of BIPOC populations and support greater participation by people from groups that have been underrepresented in arts and culture consulting.

Individuals interested in the opportunity may wish to consider whether their interests align with the programme’s focus on consulting, research, planning, and the arts and culture sector.

However, the information provided in the announcement does not set out a complete list of formal eligibility requirements. It does not specify a minimum education level, required years of experience, particular academic disciplines, or a list of eligible countries.

Applicants should therefore review the official fellowship position before applying to confirm the full eligibility criteria and any application requirements.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Lynette A. Turner Pathways to Consulting Fellowship

How to Apply for the Lynette A. Turner Pathways to Consulting Fellowship

Interested applicants should review the official fellowship position published by AMS Planning & Research.

The position page is the source provided for further details about the fellowship and how to apply:

Official fellowship position: Lynette A. Turner Pathways to Consulting Fellowship 

Applicants should carefully review the information provided on the official page, including the application process, required materials, eligibility conditions, and any instructions or deadlines.

The announcement supplied for this article does not state an application deadline. Applicants should check the official fellowship position for the current deadline and application timeline.

Application Deadline

No application deadline is stated in the announcement provided. Applicants should consult the official fellowship position for the latest application deadline and any relevant dates.

Conclusion

The Lynette A. Turner Pathways to Consulting Fellowship offers practical training, mentorship, and professional exposure for individuals seeking to explore arts and culture consulting. Through project planning, research, quantitative analysis, writing, and industry and consumer research, fellows can gain experience supporting organizations across the arts and cultural sector.

The programme also aims to address underrepresentation in the field by engaging members of BIPOC populations and helping nurture future leadership. With the option to participate in person or remotely, the fellowship provides a pathway for participants to learn from experienced professionals and develop skills relevant to consulting and the wider arts and culture sector.

Interested applicants should review the official fellowship position to confirm eligibility, application requirements, participation arrangements, and the current deadline.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the South African Institute of International Affairs (SAIIA) Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme 2027, an intensive research, policy training and mentorship initiative for emerging young researchers from across Africa and the African diaspora.

The programme is designed to help young postgraduate researchers strengthen the practical skills, professional networks and policy-research experience needed to move from university-based research into careers involving think tanks, public policy, international affairs, development research, academia, civil society and related fields.

Selected participants will travel to Johannesburg, South Africa, for an intensive week-long training workshop scheduled for 22–26 February 2027, with the dates currently listed as to be confirmed. The programme will cover participants’ travel to and from Johannesburg, accommodation and meals for the duration of the residency.

Importantly, the programme does not end when participants leave Johannesburg. Selected researchers will receive ongoing mentorship following the residency, supporting both their professional development and the production of research outputs.

SAIIA describes the Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme as a strategic capacity-building initiative that combines a youth-focused digital research platform with annual training for emerging postgraduate researchers. The programme’s broader purpose is to amplify young African voices in policy spaces and strengthen participants’ employability through research, leadership development and mentorship. SAIIA’s Youth programme states that its annual capacity-building stream brings together 20 postgraduate participants from Africa and the diaspora for intensive in-person training. SAIIA

Application deadline: 30 September 2026.

Training dates: 22–26 February 2027, subject to confirmation.

Location: Johannesburg, South Africa.

Application requirements and form: https://lnkd.in/dV2uAKQQ

About the SAIIA Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme

The South African Institute of International Affairs is one of Africa’s established international-affairs and policy-research institutions. Through the Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme, SAIIA is creating a structured pathway for younger researchers who want to strengthen the connection between academic research and practical policy engagement.

The programme grew alongside the transformation of the former Africa Portal into the Africa Youth Portal, a platform intended to give greater visibility to research and analysis produced by emerging African voices.

SAIIA describes the Africa Youth Portal as a digital hub for youth-led policy research and knowledge dissemination. Its outputs include policy briefs, web articles and blog posts, with research organized around themes including:

  • Education
  • Climate change
  • Gender
  • Peace and security
  • Youth agency and inclusion

The capacity-building component complements this publishing platform by training postgraduate researchers in the skills required to communicate research effectively to audiences beyond universities. SAIIA

A Fully Funded Week-Long Research Training Programme in Johannesburg

The centrepiece of the 2027 programme will be an intensive, in-person workshop in Johannesburg.

Proposed training dates

22–26 February 2027

The dates are currently marked TBC, meaning applicants should remain attentive to any confirmation or schedule changes communicated by SAIIA.

The residency is expected to bring together young researchers from different countries, disciplines and postgraduate levels for concentrated training, peer exchange and professional development.

One of the key strengths of the initiative is that participants are not expected to finance the Johannesburg component themselves.

The project will cover:

  • Travel to Johannesburg
  • Return travel from Johannesburg
  • Accommodation during the programme
  • Meals during the training period

This substantially reduces the financial barriers that can prevent emerging African researchers from participating in international research-training and networking opportunities.

How Many Researchers Participate?

SAIIA’s programme framework states that the annual capacity-building stream trains 20 postgraduate students from across Africa and the African diaspora through a competitive selection process.

The small cohort structure is intended to enable more intensive interaction among:

  • Participants
  • SAIIA researchers
  • Mentors
  • Policy professionals
  • Other invited experts

Rather than functioning as a large conference, the programme is structured around focused training and sustained professional development.

From Academic Research to Policy Research

One of the central purposes of the Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme is helping young researchers understand the difference between producing research mainly for academic audiences and producing research that can influence policymakers, practitioners and public debate.

Previous SAIIA programme material identifies training areas such as:

  • Differences between think-tank and academic research
  • Writing concise and influential policy pieces
  • Research dissemination
  • Media engagement
  • Digital tools for researchers
  • Artificial intelligence tools
  • Personal branding
  • Career mapping

The programme is therefore particularly useful for participants who may already have strong academic skills but want to learn how to communicate evidence in formats commonly used by policy institutions.

Why Policy Writing Is Different From Academic Writing

Many postgraduate students become familiar with long-form academic assignments, dissertations and journal-style writing.

Policy organizations frequently require a different style.

Researchers may need to communicate:

  • What happened
  • Why it matters
  • Which stakeholders are affected
  • What evidence supports the analysis
  • What the implications are
  • What policymakers should pay attention to

and do so in far fewer words.

The Africa Youth Portal programme is designed to help participants develop this type of concise, accessible and policy-relevant communication.

Research Dissemination and Media Engagement

Producing good research is only one part of becoming an effective policy researcher.

Researchers also need to understand how to communicate their findings to different audiences.

The programme’s emphasis on dissemination and media engagement can help participants think about how the same evidence might need to be presented differently to:

  • Academic researchers
  • Government officials
  • Civil society organizations
  • Journalists
  • International organizations
  • Development practitioners
  • Young audiences
  • The general public

This ability to translate complex research into accessible formats is increasingly important for researchers seeking careers outside exclusively academic environments.

AI and Digital Tools for Researchers

SAIIA’s programme has also included training on AI and digital tools for researchers. SAIIA

This reflects the rapidly changing research environment in which young analysts increasingly need to understand digital tools while maintaining strong standards of:

  • Research integrity
  • Source verification
  • Critical analysis
  • Responsible use of technology
  • Independent judgment

Applicants should nevertheless carefully follow the instructions in the 2027 application form regarding the use of AI in preparing application responses.

Personal Branding and Career Development

Academic programmes often focus heavily on research skills but provide less guidance on professional positioning.

The Africa Youth Portal programme also considers how young researchers can build careers around their expertise.

This can include thinking about:

  • How to communicate research interests professionally
  • How to develop a coherent research profile
  • How to use LinkedIn and other professional platforms
  • How to build a publication portfolio
  • How to approach think tanks and policy institutions
  • How to communicate with prospective employers
  • How to identify longer-term career pathways

This makes the programme relevant not only to future academics but also to researchers seeking careers in policy institutions, NGOs, government, international organizations and consulting.

Ongoing Mentorship After the Johannesburg Residency

A particularly important feature of the programme is the mentorship component.

Participants will not simply attend a week of training and then leave the programme.

Following the Johannesburg residency, they will receive ongoing mentorship intended to support their professional development and research outputs.

SAIIA describes mentorship as an integral part of the programme and draws on its network of experienced researchers and policy professionals to support emerging researchers.

This continued relationship may help participants:

  • Refine research ideas
  • Strengthen analytical writing
  • Improve research outputs
  • Navigate early research careers
  • Understand professional policy environments
  • Develop stronger publication strategies

Opportunity to Develop Publishable Research

The Africa Youth Portal is intended to provide a platform where emerging African researchers can contribute policy-focused work.

SAIIA’s programme model includes opportunities for participants to produce research for publication through the Portal. The platform publishes formats such as policy briefs, web articles and blogs.

For an early-career researcher, this can be particularly useful because employers frequently want evidence of actual analytical output rather than academic qualifications alone.

A publication can help demonstrate an applicant’s ability to:

  • Develop a clear research question
  • Analyze evidence
  • Write concisely
  • Communicate to a non-academic audience
  • Connect research to policy debates

Who Should Apply?

The programme is targeted primarily at young postgraduate researchers and emerging scholars interested in building research and policy careers.

Applicants who may find the programme particularly relevant include:

  • Honours students
  • Master’s students
  • PhD candidates
  • Recent postgraduate graduates
  • Emerging policy researchers
  • Early-career African scholars

The current call specifically emphasizes researchers from across the African continent and the diaspora.

Applicants should be interested in using research to engage with public-policy, development and societal challenges affecting Africa.

Age and Career Stage

The programme’s established eligibility framework has targeted young researchers between 18 and 35 years old, and current information circulating with the 2027 call continues to identify this age group as the target population. The programme is intended for researchers who are still at an early stage of their academic or professional careers.

Applicants should consult the current 2027 application form to confirm all final eligibility conditions before submitting.

Postgraduate Study Requirements

The programme is aimed at applicants who are:

  • Currently enrolled in a postgraduate programme; or
  • Recently completed postgraduate study.

Relevant levels include:

  • Honours
  • Master’s
  • PhD

Current 2027 opportunity information indicates that recent graduates should generally have completed their postgraduate programme within the previous year.

Applicants should provide the relevant academic documentation requested in the application form.

Relevant Academic Fields

The programme is multidisciplinary.

Previous and current programme information identifies fields connected to areas such as:

  • Political Science
  • International Relations
  • Journalism
  • Development Studies
  • Sociology
  • Law
  • Economics
  • Foresight Studies
  • Public Policy and related areas

The central consideration is not simply the name of the degree but whether the applicant demonstrates the ability and motivation to contribute meaningful policy-oriented research on African issues.

Applicants should use the current application guidance as the final authority regarding eligible disciplines.

Africa and the Diaspora

One important update to earlier descriptions of the programme is its explicit emphasis on both:

Researchers based across the African continent and researchers from the African diaspora.

SAIIA’s own Youth programme describes the annual training stream as bringing together postgraduate participants from “the continent and the diaspora.”

African researchers currently studying or living outside the continent should therefore not automatically assume that being abroad makes them ineligible.

The application form should be consulted for the exact citizenship or nationality documentation required.

Research Themes

The Africa Youth Portal organizes its research engagement around several broad themes.

These include:

Education

Research examining educational systems, access, skills, inequality, youth transitions and the relationship between education and African development.

Climate Change

Work examining climate policy, adaptation, mitigation, climate justice, resilience and the social and economic consequences of environmental change.

Gender

Research focusing on gender equality, inclusion, representation, social norms and gendered dimensions of development and public policy.

Peace and Security

Research considering armed conflict, peacebuilding, security governance and related political challenges.

Youth Agency and Inclusion

Research examining young people not simply as beneficiaries of policy but as political, economic and social actors capable of influencing decisions affecting their communities.

SAIIA identifies these themes as the core subject areas around which Africa Youth Portal outputs are organized. SAIIA

Application Documents to Prepare

Applicants should prepare their supporting documents before beginning the application.

Current 2027 application information indicates that candidates should have the following documents available in PDF format:

  1. Curriculum Vitae
  2. Copy of ID or passport
  3. Academic transcript or proof of enrolment
  4. Recommendation letter
  5. Proposed research topic
  6. Writing sample

Current application guidance also advises candidates to prepare everything before beginning because the online form may not save unfinished progress. Opportunity For Africa

Curriculum Vitae

Your CV should emphasize experiences relevant to research and policy.

Depending on your background, these could include:

  • Academic research
  • Thesis or dissertation work
  • Research assistantships
  • Publications
  • Policy writing
  • Conferences
  • Volunteer research
  • Youth leadership
  • Civil society involvement
  • Internships
  • Data analysis
  • Journalism
  • Advocacy
  • International affairs activities

Do not assume that lack of formal employment makes you uncompetitive.

The programme is specifically designed for emerging researchers.

Proposed Research Topic

Applicants should think carefully about the research topic they propose.

A strong topic should ideally:

  • Address an identifiable African policy problem
  • Be specific enough to research meaningfully
  • Fit the Africa Youth Portal’s thematic areas
  • Have clear contemporary relevance
  • Be capable of producing a focused policy-oriented output

A broad subject such as “climate change in Africa” is unlikely to be as effective as a clearly defined question addressing a particular country, population, institution or policy challenge.

Writing Sample

The writing sample is an opportunity to demonstrate how you think as a researcher.

Depending on the application instructions, a suitable sample could come from:

  • Dissertation work
  • Academic essays
  • Journal articles
  • Research reports
  • Policy briefs
  • Published commentary

Current information on the call indicates that applicants should prepare a sample demonstrating research and analytical ability. Opportunity For Africa

Candidates should prioritize clarity and analytical strength rather than trying to make the writing unnecessarily complicated.

Recommendation Letter

Applicants should also prepare a recommendation letter.

Where possible, select someone who can speak directly about your:

  • Research ability
  • Academic potential
  • Reliability
  • Analytical skills
  • Capacity for independent work
  • Interest in policy research

An academic supervisor, lecturer or research manager who genuinely knows your work may generally provide a more useful reference than a prominent person who knows little about your research abilities.

Full Participation Is Important

Applicants should only apply if they are able to attend the entire Johannesburg training period.

The provisional programme dates are:

22–26 February 2027

Because these dates are still marked TBC, selected applicants should remain flexible until SAIIA formally confirms the schedule.

Participants should also be prepared for post-residency mentorship and research engagements, since the programme extends beyond the five-day workshop.

What the Programme Covers

For the Johannesburg training component, the project covers:

  • Travel to Johannesburg
  • Return travel
  • Accommodation
  • Meals

Applicants should avoid assuming that unrelated personal expenses are covered unless SAIIA specifically confirms them.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted through the programme’s online application process.

Applicants are strongly advised to prepare all required materials before opening the application form.

Application requirements and form:
https://lnkd.in/dV2uAKQQ

Because the application may require several uploaded documents and research-related responses, candidates should not wait until the final day to start preparing.

Application Deadline

The deadline for the 2027 Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme is:

30 September 2026.

Applicants should submit before the deadline and should not assume that incomplete applications can be corrected afterward.

Key Programme Details at a Glance

Programme: Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme 2027

Host: South African Institute of International Affairs

Location: Johannesburg, South Africa

Training dates: 22–26 February 2027, TBC

Format: Week-long in-person training followed by ongoing mentorship

Target group: Emerging young postgraduate researchers from Africa and the African diaspora

Annual cohort: 20 postgraduate participants according to SAIIA’s programme framework SAIIA

Funding: Travel to and from Johannesburg, accommodation and meals covered

Major focus: Research skills, policy research, communication and professional development

Research themes: Education, climate change, gender, peace and security, and youth agency and inclusion SAIIA

Application deadline: 30 September 2026

Application information:
https://lnkd.in/dV2uAKQQ

Why the Africa Youth Portal Research Programme Matters

The transition between postgraduate study and a professional research career can be difficult.

A student may leave university knowing how to conduct academic research but still have little experience with:

  • Policy briefs
  • Think-tank writing
  • Media engagement
  • Professional research networks
  • Publishing for non-academic audiences
  • Translating research into practical policy insights

The Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme is designed to address precisely this gap.

SAIIA’s broader Youth programme combines policy research, policy engagement and capacity building, while the Africa Youth Portal provides a platform through which emerging African voices can contribute directly to policy discussions. SAIIA

The combination of fully supported travel, intensive training, mentorship, publication-oriented research and continental networking makes the programme particularly relevant to young African researchers seeking to move from academic study toward a sustained professional research career.

Conclusion

The SAIIA Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme 2027 offers emerging researchers from across Africa and the African diaspora an opportunity to strengthen the practical skills needed to build careers in research and public policy.

Selected participants will attend an intensive week-long workshop in Johannesburg from 22–26 February 2027, subject to confirmation, while the project covers travel, accommodation and meals.

The residency is only the beginning. Participants will continue receiving mentorship following the training, helping them strengthen their research outputs and professional development.

Through the wider Africa Youth Portal, SAIIA is also creating a platform for young researchers to communicate policy-relevant ideas to audiences beyond academia. The programme’s annual training stream brings together 20 postgraduate researchers and focuses on research methodologies, publishing, digital tools, personal branding and media engagement. SAIIA

For postgraduate researchers who want to move from academic research toward think-tank work, policy analysis, international affairs or other evidence-based careers, the 2027 programme provides a structured opportunity to develop those skills while joining a pan-African research network.

Applications close on 30 September 2026.

Apply and review the requirements:
https://lnkd.in/dV2uAKQQ

item.content:encoded:
Researchers working in low- and middle-income countries in Africa and Asia can apply for the PAIE Scholars Program, an initiative designed to help researchers develop rigorous, policy-relevant research on how artificial intelligence can be used for social good and in the fight against poverty.

The program, offered through Project AI Evidence (PAIE), an initiative of the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL), combines specialized training, research concept development, assessment, potential research mentorship, proposal-development and travel support, and the possibility of substantial pilot research funding.

Selected scholars will receive training in randomized evaluation and the evaluation of AI-enabled interventions. Those who successfully complete the first phase of the program will receive a US$1,000 award. Scholars who progress through the competitive subsequent stages may also receive a proposal-development and travel grant of up to US$10,000, research mentorship, and eventually the opportunity to compete for up to US$75,000 in PAIE pilot funding.

The PAIE Scholars Program therefore provides a structured pathway for researchers who want to turn an early research idea involving artificial intelligence into a rigorous evaluation capable of generating evidence relevant to policy and social outcomes.

About the PAIE Scholars Program

The PAIE Scholars Program supports researchers based in low- and middle-income countries in Asia and Africa who are interested in developing and leading rigorous evaluations of innovative applications of artificial intelligence for social good and poverty reduction.

The program is built around the idea that AI-enabled interventions need rigorous evidence to understand whether, how, and under what circumstances they produce meaningful social or economic outcomes.

Rather than requiring applicants to arrive with a fully developed research project, the program allows researchers to begin with a working concept note. Participants then refine their research ideas throughout the training, incorporating methodological knowledge and feedback from the PAIE team.

The program is particularly focused on connecting research ideas involving AI with rigorous evaluation methods, including randomized evaluations.

According to the program structure, successful scholars can progress through several stages, beginning with training and assessment and potentially moving toward proposal development, research mentorship, and pilot funding. However, advancement from one stage to another is competitive, and selection for the initial cohort does not automatically guarantee subsequent support or funding.

What Does the PAIE Scholars Program Offer?

The program provides several forms of support at different stages.

1. Specialized Research Training

Selected scholars will participate in structured training covering:

  • Randomized evaluation methods.
  • Evaluation of AI-enabled interventions.
  • Research design and evidence generation.
  • Materials related to AI evaluation.
  • Relevant methodological readings and learning resources.
  • Live online workshops.
  • A PAIE-administered assessment.

The training includes selected modules from J-PAL 102x: Designing and Running Randomized Evaluations, which forms part of the MITx MicroMasters in Data, Economics, and Design of Policy.

Participants will also engage with the AI Evidence Playbook, the AI Evaluation Playbook, and related reading materials.

The program will include live online workshops focused specifically on evaluating AI-enabled interventions.

2. US$1,000 Award

Scholars who successfully complete the first phase of the program will receive a US$1,000 award.

The award is conditional on meeting the requirements of the first phase. Specifically, scholars must complete their assigned training requirements, pass the PAIE-administered assessment, and submit a revised concept note that meets the program requirements.

The US$1,000 award is separate from any later proposal-development and travel support.

Importantly, receiving this award does not automatically guarantee research mentorship, pilot funding, or advancement to subsequent stages.

3. Concept Note Development

Applicants will enter the program with a working concept note submitted during the application process.

The concept note does not have to represent a fully developed research project. Applicants also do not need to have an implementing partner at the initial application stage.

During the training, scholars will refine their concept notes using what they learn from the program.

The revised concept note will form the basis for consideration for proposal-development and travel support and potential research mentorship.

The revised concept note is expected to address areas such as:

  • The policy or social problem motivating the proposed research.
  • The AI-enabled intervention or policy application being considered.
  • The research question.
  • Why rigorous evidence is necessary.
  • The relevant population and research setting.
  • The scholar’s initial evaluation design.
  • Potential outcomes and data sources.
  • A potential implementing partner, if one has been identified.
  • An initial strategy for identifying an implementing partner if one has not yet been identified.
  • The pathway toward a randomized evaluation.
  • What a potential pilot study would establish.
  • Further research-development needs.
  • How proposal-development and travel support would be used.

4. Proposal-Development and Travel Grant of Up to US$10,000

Scholars selected for the next stage may receive a proposal-development and travel grant of up to US$10,000.

This support is designed to help researchers transform their preliminary research ideas into full pilot proposals.

The grant can support activities such as:

  • Conducting background research.
  • Identifying or developing relationships with potential implementing partners.
  • Visiting potential field research sites.
  • Assessing the availability and suitability of existing administrative or survey data.
  • Conducting preliminary analysis of existing data where such analysis does not constitute human-subjects research.
  • Refining the research question.
  • Improving the evaluation design.
  • Preparing a pilot proposal.
  • Developing the research budget.

However, the proposal-development and travel grant cannot be used to conduct human-subjects research or collect data from research participants.

5. Potential Research Mentorship

Researchers who receive proposal-development support may also receive research mentorship, depending on their needs and the availability of appropriate mentors.

Mentors may include J-PAL-affiliated professors or invited researchers with relevant methodological or subject-matter expertise.

Mentorship may cover areas such as:

  • Refining the research question.
  • Developing the evaluation design.
  • Establishing or strengthening implementing partnerships.
  • Preparing for fieldwork.
  • Developing the pilot proposal.
  • Strengthening the overall research strategy.

PAIE staff and the J-PAL research team may also provide additional support during the proposal-development process.

However, receiving research mentorship or a proposal-development and travel grant does not guarantee subsequent pilot funding.

PAIE Pilot Funding of Up to US$75,000

One of the later stages of the program provides an opportunity for eligible scholars to submit a full proposal for an early-stage pilot study.

Scholars may reach this stage after completing the proposal-development process or, where a project is already sufficiently developed, they may be invited to proceed directly to a full pilot proposal.

The pilot research should have a clear research question and be designed to develop into, or inform, a future full-scale randomized evaluation.

Successful pilot research could be used to:

  • Test the feasibility of an AI-enabled intervention.
  • Test aspects of the proposed research design.
  • Refine measurement strategies.
  • Develop implementation and research logistics.
  • Collect pilot data.
  • Facilitate access to administrative data.
  • Generate information needed to design a larger randomized evaluation.
  • Build evidence that could potentially inform policy at scale.

By the pilot-proposal stage, researchers are expected to have an implementing partner and a sufficiently developed research design.

Pilot proposals will undergo a separate competitive review. Successful proposals may receive up to US$75,000 in PAIE pilot funding.

Being invited to submit a pilot proposal does not guarantee that funding will ultimately be awarded.

Who Is Eligible for the PAIE Scholars Program?

The PAIE Scholars Program is specifically designed for resident scholars based in low- and middle-income countries in Asia and Africa, according to the World Bank’s classification.

For this program, a resident scholar is a researcher who:

  • Has completed a PhD.
  • Has a primary professional affiliation with a university located in an eligible country.
  • May hold additional positions at other organizations, provided that the primary university affiliation is in an eligible country.

Applicants should therefore carefully check the program’s definitive list of eligible countries before applying.

Academic and Research Requirements

Applicants must satisfy several academic and professional requirements.

Completed PhD

Applicants must have completed a PhD in economics or another relevant empirical discipline.

Advanced Quantitative Training

Applicants must have advanced training in quantitative methods. Relevant areas include:

  • Statistics.
  • Econometrics.
  • Causal inference.
  • Experimental methods.
  • Machine learning.

This quantitative foundation is important because the program focuses heavily on rigorous evaluation and evidence generation.

Interest in AI Evaluation

Applicants must demonstrate an interest in evaluating how AI-enabled interventions affect social or economic outcomes.

The proposed research should therefore connect artificial intelligence with a meaningful social, economic, development, or policy question that can be investigated through rigorous empirical research.

English Proficiency

Applicants must have sufficient English proficiency to:

  • Complete the required coursework.
  • Participate in the training.
  • Complete the assessment.
  • Prepare research outputs in English.

Availability

Applicants must be willing and available to complete all required components of the program.

The initial training is tentatively expected to run for approximately three months, from November 2026 through January 2027.

Selected scholars should expect to dedicate approximately four to ten hours per week, depending on their previous training and familiarity with randomized evaluations.

The final schedule, coursework, and expected time commitment will be communicated before the program begins.

Do Applicants Need a Fully Developed Research Project?

No.

One of the important features of the PAIE Scholars Program is that applicants do not need to have a fully developed research project at the time of application.

Applicants submit a working concept note describing the research idea they would like to develop.

The concept note does not need to contain a complete intervention or evaluation design.

Applicants are also not required to have an implementing partner at the initial application stage.

This allows eligible researchers to enter the program with an early-stage idea and use the training and support provided by PAIE to strengthen that idea.

Applicants also do not need to have an existing relationship with a J-PAL-affiliated professor or invited researcher in order to apply.

What Documents Are Required?

The application requires applicants to provide information about their academic background, research experience, quantitative training, and interest in evaluating AI-enabled interventions.

Applicants will be asked to submit:

  1. A curriculum vitae (CV).
  2. One to three examples of their research.
  3. Brief statements describing:
    • Their research experience.
    • Their experience with randomized evaluations.
    • Their interest in evaluating AI-enabled interventions.
    • Their interest in participating in the PAIE Scholars Program.
  4. A working concept note describing the research idea they would like to develop and explaining how the idea could ultimately lead to a randomized evaluation.

The application form provides the complete requirements and applicable word limits.

How the PAIE Scholars Program Works

The program follows a staged process rather than providing all forms of support immediately.

Stage 1: Application

Researchers submit an online application containing their academic and research information, supporting materials, statements, and working concept note.

Stage 2: Selection

A cohort of scholars is selected to participate in the initial program.

Selection into this cohort does not guarantee progression to later stages.

Stage 3: Training

Selected scholars participate in training covering randomized evaluations and the evaluation of AI-enabled interventions.

Stage 4: Assessment

Participants complete a PAIE-administered proctored assessment based on the training.

The PAIE assessment is a requirement of the program.

It is important to distinguish this assessment from the official MITx assessment. The PAIE-administered assessment is separate and does not result in an MITx certificate.

Scholars may later complete the official MITx assessment and potentially earn an MITx certificate, subject to the applicable MITx requirements and assessment schedule.

Researchers who already have sufficient training in randomized evaluation may complete selected 102x modules.

Stage 5: Revised Concept Note

Scholars who complete their assigned training requirements and pass the PAIE assessment will submit a revised concept note.

The revised concept note becomes the basis for consideration for proposal-development and travel support and potential research mentorship.

Stage 6: Proposal Development and Mentorship

PAIE will review the revised concept notes and select a subset of scholars for proposal-development and travel support.

Depending on their needs and mentor availability, selected scholars may also receive research mentorship.

Stage 7: Full Pilot Proposal

Scholars who successfully develop their research ideas may proceed to the full pilot-proposal stage.

Researchers invited to submit a pilot proposal will need to have a sufficiently developed research design and, at this stage, an implementing partner.

Stage 8: Competitive Pilot Funding Review

Full pilot proposals undergo a separate competitive review.

Successful proposals may receive up to US$75,000 in PAIE pilot funding.

Application Deadline

The PAIE Scholars Program 2026 application deadline is October 16, 2026, at 12:00 PM Eastern Time (ET).

Applications opened on September 17, 2026.

Prospective applicants should prepare their materials well in advance of the deadline because the application requires a CV, research examples, multiple statements, and a working concept note.

PAIE Scholars Program Timeline

The current program timeline is as follows:

Activity Timeline
Applications open September 17, 2026
Application deadline October 16, 2026 at 12 PM ET
Scholars selected Early November 2026
Training begins November 2026
Initial training period Approximately November 2026–January 2027
PAIE-administered assessment To be confirmed
Revised concept notes due To be confirmed
Proposal-development grant decisions To be confirmed
Pilot-proposal timeline To be announced

Additional dates, including the pilot-proposal timeline, will be communicated to selected scholars.

Key Points Applicants Should Understand

Prospective applicants should pay attention to several important aspects of the program.

First, the program is designed specifically for researchers based in eligible low- and middle-income countries in Africa and Asia.

Second, applicants must have completed a PhD in economics or another relevant empirical discipline and possess advanced quantitative training.

Third, applicants do not need to arrive with a complete research project. A working concept note is sufficient at the application stage.

Fourth, an implementing partner is not required when initially applying. However, an implementing partner is expected by the pilot-proposal stage.

Fifth, the initial US$1,000 award is conditional on successful completion of the first phase and should not be interpreted as guaranteed funding for subsequent research.

Sixth, proposal-development and travel support of up to US$10,000 is available only to scholars selected for that stage.

Finally, pilot funding of up to US$75,000 is subject to a separate competitive review. Participation in earlier stages does not guarantee pilot funding.

Why the Working Concept Note Matters

The working concept note is an important part of the PAIE Scholars Program because it provides the starting point for the research-development process.

Applicants are not expected to have finalized every aspect of their research methodology. Instead, they should clearly communicate the research problem they want to investigate, the potential role of an AI-enabled intervention, the population and setting they are interested in, and how the idea could eventually be evaluated rigorously.

During the program, scholars will have an opportunity to improve their concept notes using the methods and knowledge gained through the training.

The revised concept note can then serve as the basis for consideration for further proposal-development support and research mentorship.

What Kind of Research Is the Program Looking For?

The program focuses on research involving innovative applications of artificial intelligence for social good and in the fight against poverty.

Applicants should therefore consider research questions that examine how AI-enabled interventions may affect social or economic outcomes and how these effects can be evaluated using rigorous empirical methods.

The program’s emphasis on randomized evaluation means that applicants should think about how their initial research idea could eventually develop into a rigorous evaluation capable of producing credible evidence.

The concept note should therefore not simply describe an AI technology. It should begin to establish a meaningful research question and a pathway toward evaluating the intervention.

About Project AI Evidence and J-PAL

The PAIE Scholars Program is part of Project AI Evidence (PAIE).

Project AI Evidence focuses on identifying, evaluating, and scaling innovative applications of artificial intelligence for social good and poverty reduction. It brings together AI adopters, technology companies, and researchers to strengthen evidence around AI applications.

PAIE is an initiative of the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL).

J-PAL’s work includes research and initiatives focused on generating evidence and using that evidence to inform policy.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should complete the official online application before the stated deadline.

The application requires information concerning the applicant’s academic background, research experience, quantitative training, and interest in evaluating AI-enabled interventions.

Applicants should prepare the required materials, including:

  • CV.
  • One to three research examples.
  • Research experience statement.
  • Randomized-evaluation experience statement.
  • Statement of interest in evaluating AI-enabled interventions.
  • Statement explaining interest in the PAIE Scholars Program.
  • Working concept note.

Applicants should also carefully review the official eligibility requirements and the definitive list of eligible countries before submitting an application.

Application deadline: October 16, 2026, at 12:00 PM ET.

CLICK HERE TO APPLY

Contact Information

Applicants with questions about the PAIE Scholars Program can contact the PAIE team by email at paie@povertyactionlab.org.

Click HERE for more information about the PAIE Scholars Program 2026.

Conclusion

The PAIE Scholars Program 2026 provides a structured research-development opportunity for eligible researchers in low- and middle-income countries in Africa and Asia who are interested in studying the social and economic effects of AI-enabled interventions.

The program goes beyond conventional research training by combining methodological instruction with concept-note development, assessment, potential research mentorship, proposal-development and travel support, and the possibility of substantial pilot research funding.

Selected scholars can receive a US$1,000 award after successfully completing the first phase. Those who progress through the subsequent competitive stage may receive up to US$10,000 in proposal-development and travel support, while successful pilot proposals may ultimately receive up to US$75,000 in PAIE pilot funding.

Because later stages are competitive, applicants should understand that participation in the initial training does not automatically lead to mentorship, proposal-development funding, or pilot funding.

For eligible researchers with a PhD, strong quantitative-methods training, and a research interest in evaluating AI-enabled interventions, the program offers a pathway for developing an early research idea into a more rigorous evaluation proposal.

Interested applicants should review the eligibility requirements, prepare the required application materials, develop a clear working concept note, and submit the application before the October 16, 2026 deadline at 12:00 PM ET.
