item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program (Trailblazers 5.0), an early-career development opportunity designed for ambitious recent graduates who are ready to accelerate their professional growth within a global organisation.

Based in Lagos-Island, Lagos, Nigeria, the programme provides successful candidates with practical exposure to Reckitt’s business through rotations across its Commercial and Supply functions. Participants will gain experience with end-to-end business processes, contribute to real business projects from the beginning of their journey, and receive mentorship from experienced business leaders.

The programme is designed to develop the next generation of Reckitt leaders, making it particularly relevant to graduates who want more than a conventional entry-level role and are interested in gaining broad, cross-functional business experience early in their careers.

About Reckitt

Reckitt is a global company behind a portfolio of well-known brands across the health, hygiene and nutrition sectors.

The company describes its purpose around protecting, healing and nurturing in pursuit of a cleaner and healthier world, with its products and brands serving consumers across international markets.

For graduates and students specifically, Reckitt offers internships, apprenticeships and graduate programmes across different locations worldwide. Its graduate programmes are designed to provide participants with practical experiences, learning opportunities and responsibility for projects involving global brands.

In Nigeria, Reckitt Benckiser (Nigeria) Ltd has an office at Heritage Place, 21 Lugard Avenue, Ikoyi, Lagos.

About the Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program

The Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program, also known as Trailblazers 5.0, provides young graduates with an accelerated pathway for developing their careers within a global organisation.

Rather than placing participants exclusively within one narrow area of the business, the programme provides exposure to end-to-end business processes through rotations across Commercial and Supply functions.

This rotational structure gives trainees the opportunity to understand how different parts of an international consumer goods business connect and operate.

Most importantly, trainees are expected to work on genuine business projects and engage with real-life business scenarios from the beginning of the programme.

This practical approach is intended to help participants move beyond theoretical knowledge gained at university and begin developing the commercial awareness, problem-solving capabilities and professional judgement needed in a corporate environment.

The programme ultimately aims to identify and develop people who could become the next generation of leaders within Reckitt.

Reckitt Nigeria Trailblazers 5.0 Program Overview

Key details of the opportunity include:

  • Programme: Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program
  • Programme name: Trailblazers 5.0
  • Company: Reckitt
  • Location: Lagos-Island, Lagos, Nigeria
  • Target group: Recent graduates
  • Eligible degree disciplines: Any degree
  • Graduation years: 2022 to 2025
  • Minimum academic requirement: Upper Second Class Honours
  • NYSC requirement: Applicants must have completed NYSC by December 2026
  • Rotational areas: Commercial and Supply functions
  • Requisition ID: 86550
  • Date posted: 19 September 2026

The vacancy is currently listed on Reckitt’s official graduate careers platform.

What Successful Trailblazers Will Experience

The Reckitt Nigeria Management Trainee Program is structured to combine professional development with hands-on business exposure.

Successful candidates can expect several important elements during their experience.

1. Cross-Functional Business Rotations

Participants will gain experience through rotations across Reckitt’s Commercial and Supply functions.

Rotational programmes can provide early-career professionals with a broader understanding of how different departments contribute to the overall organisation.

Instead of learning about only one business function, Reckitt Trailblazers will have the opportunity to gain exposure to different parts of the company’s operations and understand the connections between them.

2. Exposure to End-to-End Business Processes

Reckitt specifically highlights exposure to end-to-end business processes as an important component of the programme.

This means participants can gain a broader perspective on how activities across different business functions contribute to Reckitt’s operations.

For a recent graduate, such exposure can be valuable in building commercial awareness and understanding how decisions made in one part of a business may influence another.

3. Work on Real Business Projects

Trailblazers will not simply observe experienced employees at work.

Reckitt states that participants will have opportunities to work on business projects and real-life business scenarios from Day One.

This gives successful applicants an opportunity to begin applying their academic knowledge, analytical capabilities, communication skills and problem-solving abilities in a professional environment.

4. Work With Major Consumer Brands

Successful applicants will have the opportunity to build their careers while working within the organisation behind some of the world’s recognised health, hygiene and nutrition brands.

Reckitt describes itself as a global organisation focused on delivering better health to more people through its portfolio and operations.

5. Mentorship From Business Leaders

Another significant element of the Trailblazers 5.0 programme is mentorship.

Reckitt states that participants will have opportunities to be mentored by its business leaders.

For recent graduates transitioning from university into a corporate environment, access to experienced professionals can provide valuable guidance while they develop their understanding of business operations, workplace expectations and leadership.

Who Can Apply for the Reckitt Nigeria Management Trainee Program?

Reckitt has outlined specific eligibility requirements for candidates interested in becoming part of Trailblazers 5.0.

Applicants should carefully review these requirements before submitting an application.

Recent Graduate Requirement

Applicants must be recent graduates who completed their studies between 2022 and 2025.

This makes the programme particularly suitable for individuals who are in the early stages of their professional careers.

Degree Requirement

Reckitt states that it is open to graduates from any degree discipline.

Therefore, applicants are not restricted to a specific academic subject such as business, marketing, engineering or supply chain.

This broad degree eligibility opens the opportunity to graduates from a variety of academic backgrounds, provided they satisfy the other programme requirements.

Academic Classification

Applicants must have graduated with at least an Upper Second Class Honours degree.

Candidates should therefore ensure that their academic qualification satisfies this requirement before applying.

NYSC Requirement

Candidates must have completed the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) programme by December 2026.

This is a particularly important eligibility requirement for applicants to note.

Candidates who have already completed NYSC or will complete it by the specified December 2026 timeframe can consider applying, provided they meet the programme’s other requirements.

What Kind of Candidate Is Reckitt Looking For?

Academic qualifications alone are not the only consideration.

Reckitt describes its ideal Nigeria Trailblazer as someone who is:

  • Curious
  • Driven
  • Ambitious

These qualities align with the nature of a management trainee programme where participants are expected to learn quickly, adapt to different business environments and contribute to practical projects.

Reckitt also states that it considers potential alongside experience and encourages candidates who believe the organisation and role are a good fit to consider applying even if they do not feel they meet every point in the job description.

Skills Needed to Succeed in Trailblazers 5.0

Reckitt identifies several capabilities as important for success in the programme.

Ownership

Participants should be prepared to take responsibility for their work and contribution.

Working on genuine business projects from the beginning means trainees may need to demonstrate accountability and a willingness to take initiative.

Self-Awareness

The ability to understand personal strengths, development areas and behaviour can be particularly important in a rotational environment where participants may encounter different teams, responsibilities and working styles.

Mental Agility

Participants should be capable of adapting their thinking as they encounter new situations and business challenges.

This may be especially relevant when moving between different functions during the programme.

Proactiveness

Rather than waiting to be directed at every stage, successful trainees are expected to demonstrate initiative and an active approach to learning and contributing.

Communication Skills

Effective communication is important when collaborating with colleagues, managers and stakeholders across different parts of an organisation.

Attention to Detail

Candidates should be capable of maintaining accuracy and carefully considering details while working on business assignments and projects.

Analytical Skills

The ability to examine information, identify patterns and draw useful conclusions can help trainees approach business challenges more effectively.

Problem-Solving Skills

As participants will encounter real business scenarios, they should be comfortable identifying problems, considering possible solutions and contributing to practical outcomes.

Together, Reckitt lists ownership, self-awareness, mental agility, proactiveness, communication, attention to detail, analytical ability and problem-solving among the skills associated with success in the role.

Why Consider a Graduate Programme at Reckitt?

Reckitt describes its graduate programmes more broadly as opportunities that allow participants to develop quickly through a range of experiences and learning opportunities.

Graduates can be trusted with responsibility and opportunities to work on projects associated with global brands while developing their careers within the organisation.

For participants in Nigeria’s Trailblazers 5.0 programme specifically, the combination of Commercial and Supply rotations, practical projects, real-world business scenarios and mentorship creates a development-focused early-career experience.

Employee Benefits and Support at Reckitt

Beyond professional development, Reckitt highlights a broader employee support framework.

The company states that inclusion is an important part of its workplace approach and that it works alongside four global Employee Resource Groups to support employees throughout their careers.

Benefits and support highlighted by Reckitt include:

  • Parental benefits
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Life insurance for employees globally
  • Additional benefits according to the applicable local market
  • Global share plans
  • Short-term incentives for eligible positions
  • Career support and development

The precise benefits available to an individual employee may depend on the role, eligibility requirements, location and applicable company policies.

Reckitt also states that its reward approach follows a pay-for-performance philosophy.

Reckitt’s Approach to Inclusion and Equal Opportunity

Reckitt states that qualified applicants are considered for employment without discrimination based on protected characteristics.

The company also acknowledges that strong candidates may not always meet every single point in a job description and states that it hires for potential as well as experience.

This approach is especially relevant in an early-career programme where applicants may have limited professional experience but demonstrate strong potential, ambition and transferable capabilities.

How to Apply for the Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program

Interested candidates should submit their applications through Reckitt’s official careers platform.

Applicants can follow these general steps:

  1. Visit the official Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program vacancy.
  2. Review the complete programme description and eligibility requirements.
  3. Select the application option on the vacancy page.
  4. Sign in or create the required candidate profile if prompted.
  5. Complete all requested personal, educational and professional information accurately.
  6. Upload any requested supporting documents.
  7. Review the application carefully before submission.
  8. Submit the application through Reckitt’s recruitment system.

Applicants should ensure that their application information accurately demonstrates how they satisfy the academic, graduation-year and NYSC requirements.

Official application page: Apply for the Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program

Application Deadline

The official Reckitt vacancy reviewed for this article does not currently state a specific application deadline.

Some third-party opportunity and recruitment websites list 10 October 2026 as the closing date. However, because this date is not currently displayed on Reckitt’s official vacancy page, applicants should not rely exclusively on the third-party deadline.

Interested candidates are therefore strongly encouraged to apply as early as possible while the official vacancy remains open and monitor the Reckitt careers page for any changes to the recruitment timeline.

Important Information for Applicants

Before submitting an application, candidates should pay particular attention to the following:

  • The opportunity is specifically advertised as the Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program (Trailblazers 5.0).
  • The advertised location is Lagos-Island, Lagos, Nigeria.
  • Applicants can come from any degree discipline.
  • Candidates must have graduated between 2022 and 2025.
  • A minimum Upper Second Class Honours degree is required.
  • Candidates must have completed NYSC by December 2026.
  • Reckitt is looking for candidates who demonstrate curiosity, ambition and drive.
  • Applicants should demonstrate skills including communication, analytical thinking, problem-solving, ownership, proactiveness and attention to detail.
  • Applications should be submitted through the official Reckitt careers platform.

APPLY NOW

Conclusion

The Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program (Trailblazers 5.0) presents an early-career opportunity for recent graduates seeking practical exposure within a global health, hygiene and nutrition business.

Through rotations across Commercial and Supply functions, participants will have an opportunity to develop an understanding of end-to-end business processes while contributing to real projects and business scenarios from the beginning of their journey.

The combination of cross-functional exposure, practical responsibilities and mentorship from experienced business leaders makes the programme particularly relevant to ambitious graduates who want to develop their commercial, analytical, communication, problem-solving and leadership capabilities.

Candidates who graduated between 2022 and 2025, hold at least an Upper Second Class Honours degree, and will have completed NYSC by December 2026 should review the complete requirements and consider submitting an application while the official vacancy remains available.

Applicants should use Reckitt’s official recruitment platform for the latest programme information and application instructions.

Visit the OFY website for more Job Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program 2027 in Hamburg, Germany, offering accomplished researchers and scholars an opportunity to pursue independent research in the fields of peace, security, political violence, European security, emerging technologies, climate security, and related interdisciplinary areas.

Jointly offered by the Hamburg Institute for Advanced Study (HIAS) and the Institute for Peace Research and Security Policy at the University of Hamburg (IFSH), the fellowship provides selected scholars with the opportunity to live and work in Hamburg while advancing an independent research project within an interdisciplinary and internationally connected academic environment.

The fellowship is designed primarily for outstanding scholars who have completed a doctorate and demonstrated substantial academic achievement. However, applications from artists, policymakers, and other professionals may also be considered when their work is closely connected to the fellowship’s research priorities and engages substantively with scholarly inquiry.

Selected fellows will benefit from financial support, a fully equipped workspace, interdisciplinary academic exchange, connections to Hamburg’s research community, an IFSH academic tandem partner, and support with accommodation and family arrangements.

The application deadline is November 16, 2026, and the earliest possible fellowship start date is October 2027.

About the HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program

The Joint Fellowship Program brings together the resources and intellectual communities of HIAS and IFSH to provide researchers with an environment where they can develop innovative ideas and pursue ambitious research projects.

IFSH is a Hamburg-based research institution specialising in peace and security studies. Through the fellowship, researchers can work within an environment focused on contemporary questions surrounding peace, conflict, security, resilience, political violence, international relations, technology, and societal change.

At the same time, fellows become part of the interdisciplinary community at HIAS, where internationally renowned researchers and professionals from a wide range of academic backgrounds come together.

The program is particularly interested in applicants who demonstrate:

  • Significant academic achievements;
  • Intellectual curiosity;
  • An interdisciplinary and international research profile;
  • Strong interest in interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary exchange;
  • Willingness to cooperate with researchers at IFSH and fellows at HIAS; and
  • Interest in communicating their research beyond specialised academic audiences.

Applicants are also encouraged to consider how their proposed projects could contribute to broader public understanding of their research topic.

Research Areas for the 2027 Fellowship

The HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program particularly welcomes research projects addressing, or closely connected to, several major areas of peace and security research.

1. Societal Perspectives on Peace and Security

Researchers working on the relationship between societies, political systems, violence, radicalisation, and security are encouraged to apply.

Relevant subjects include:

  • Societal perspectives on peace and security;
  • Political violence;
  • Fascism;
  • Political and societal polarisation;
  • Radicalisation;
  • Counterterrorism; and
  • Related social and political developments affecting peace and security.

Projects that investigate these issues through innovative or interdisciplinary approaches are particularly encouraged.

2. Great Power Conflict, Arms Dynamics and Emerging Technologies

The fellowship also welcomes researchers examining international strategic competition and the changing technological dimensions of security.

Relevant areas include:

  • Great power conflict;
  • Arms dynamics;
  • Deterrence;
  • Strategic stability;
  • Emerging technologies;
  • Cybersecurity; and
  • Related developments affecting international peace and security.

Researchers may explore how technological transformation influences military strategy, international competition, deterrence relationships, institutional responses, and the wider international security environment.

3. European Security and Regional Security Architecture

European security is another major area of interest.

Relevant research topics include:

  • European security architecture;
  • European regional security organisations;
  • The future of European security; and
  • Broader questions concerning institutions, cooperation, conflict, and security arrangements within Europe.

Projects may examine existing security structures as well as emerging challenges and possible transformations in European security.

4. Climate Change, Crisis Resilience and Civil Protection

The fellowship additionally encourages projects examining the relationship between environmental change, crises, resilience, and security.

Relevant subjects include:

  • Climate change and security;
  • Polycrisis;
  • Disaster response;
  • Disaster preparedness;
  • Crisis resilience;
  • Civil protection; and
  • Related interdisciplinary approaches to contemporary security challenges.

Projects that connect these subjects with perspectives from different academic disciplines are especially welcome.

Interdisciplinary Research Is Strongly Encouraged

A major characteristic of the HIAS and IFSH fellowship is its emphasis on interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary research.

Applicants are therefore encouraged to propose projects that benefit from interaction across different fields of study.

The selection process considers whether a project:

  • Opens up new research questions or ways of thinking;
  • Benefits from engagement with other disciplines;
  • Addresses issues relevant to the fellowship’s core research areas;
  • Is suitable for an Institute for Advanced Study environment;
  • Can be connected with an appropriate academic tandem partner at IFSH; and
  • Can realistically be undertaken within the research environment available through HIAS, IFSH, and Hamburg.

Who Can Apply for the HIAS and IFSH Fellowship?

The program is primarily intended for accomplished scholars with strong academic records.

For applicants working in academia, a doctorate is mandatory.

The minimum academic requirement is a doctorate in one of the following broad areas:

  • Humanities;
  • Social sciences;
  • Natural sciences; or
  • Life sciences.

Candidates should demonstrate an academic and research profile relevant to the fellowship.

Selection criteria include:

  • A completed doctorate;
  • Publications in relevant academic journals or comparable publication outlets;
  • An interdisciplinary and international research profile;
  • Relevant research experience connected with the fellowship’s core research areas;
  • Prestigious prizes and awards, where applicable; and
  • A very good command of English.

The fellowship takes applicants’ career stages into consideration and places particular emphasis on the future potential of early-career researchers.

Opportunities for Artists, Policymakers and Other Professionals

Although the program is strongly research-oriented, eligibility is not necessarily limited to conventional academic career paths.

Applications from artists, policymakers, and other professionals may also be considered.

Their work must, however:

  • Be closely connected to the fellowship’s research focus; and
  • Engage substantively with scholarly inquiry.

This allows the fellowship to incorporate perspectives beyond traditional academia while maintaining a strong connection to rigorous intellectual and research-based work.

Commitment to Equal Opportunities and Diversity

HIAS and IFSH are committed to equal opportunities and actively encourage applications from groups that may be underrepresented within research and academia.

The fellowship particularly welcomes applications from:

  • Female scholars;
  • Non-binary scholars;
  • Early-career researchers; and
  • Individuals from regions that are usually underrepresented in research and academia.

The fellowship also considers diversity when forming the broader group of scholars at IFSH and each cohort of fellows at HIAS.

Factors considered include diversity in:

  • Academic disciplines;
  • Countries of origin;
  • Gender; and
  • Career stages.

Applicants From the Hamburg Metropolitan Region Are Not Eligible

The fellowship is intended to bring scholars and professionals into the Hamburg research environment.

For this reason, applicants from within the metropolitan region of Hamburg are not eligible.

Fellows are expected to live and work in Hamburg for the duration of their fellowship.

Consequently, proposed projects must be suitable for being undertaken on-site at HIAS and IFSH.

Applicants seeking a fully remote fellowship arrangement should therefore note that the program requires physical presence in Hamburg.

Fellowship Duration and Dates

The HIAS and IFSH academic year generally runs from:

October 1 to June 30 of the following year.

The earliest possible starting date is October 2027.

Applicants must indicate their preferred fellowship period when submitting their application.

The proposed stay must last:

  • A minimum of three months; and
  • A maximum of nine months.

Applicants should also note that:

July, August, and September are not fellowship months.

Candidates should take these restrictions into account when proposing their preferred period of residence.

Financial Support

The fellowship is funded by IFSH.

Funding can be provided through either:

  • A stipend paid to the fellow; or
  • Reimbursement of the fellow’s home institution for the cost of a teaching replacement.

Applicants are also encouraged to explore whether their home institutions can provide financial support during the fellowship.

This could include arrangements such as:

  • A sabbatical;
  • Paid research leave; or
  • Other forms of institutional financial contribution.

Any possible financial contribution from an applicant’s home institution is highly encouraged and should be mentioned in the application.

Independent Research and Academic Freedom

One of the principal advantages of the fellowship is the freedom given to fellows to pursue their own research.

Selected fellows can work independently on their proposed projects while benefiting from interdisciplinary intellectual exchange within the communities of HIAS and IFSH.

This structure provides researchers with time and space to concentrate on their projects while remaining connected to scholars from other disciplines and research traditions.

Fully Equipped Workspace in Hamburg

Fellows receive access to a fully equipped workspace in central Hamburg.

They also benefit from ongoing support from the HIAS and IFSH teams throughout their stay.

The working environment is intended to provide fellows with the practical resources and institutional support necessary to focus on their research and participate fully in the fellowship community.

IFSH Academic Tandem Partner

Every fellow is expected to collaborate with an academic tandem partner based at IFSH.

The tandem structure is an important component of the fellowship.

Through their IFSH tandem partner, fellows can gain access to:

  • Relevant local academic networks;
  • Research infrastructure;
  • Institutional expertise;
  • Potential collaborators; and
  • Knowledge of Hamburg’s wider research environment.

Applicants are asked to identify possible academic tandem partners from IFSH in their application.

However, applicants do not need to have established contact with the potential tandem partner before applying.

Simply naming an appropriate potential tandem partner is sufficient.

A letter of intent is requested only when the applicant and prospective tandem partner already know each other and intend to collaborate.

Access to HIAS Member Institutions

In addition to the collaboration available through IFSH, HIAS will assist fellows in identifying and connecting with potential cooperation partners at one of its ten member institutions.

This provides fellows with opportunities to broaden their research networks and identify relevant scholars, expertise, or resources within Hamburg’s wider academic community.

Academic Program and Mandatory Participation

The fellowship involves more than independent research.

Fellows are expected to participate actively in the academic life of HIAS.

Mandatory activities include:

  • Weekly lunches; and
  • Colloquia and dinners at HIAS.

Fellows may also participate in additional excursions organised as part of the program.

Active participation in the academic program is mandatory, reflecting the fellowship’s emphasis on intellectual exchange and community building.

Family-Friendly Fellowship in Hamburg

HIAS and IFSH recognise that researchers may relocate with their families during longer research stays.

Selected fellows may therefore have access to accommodation in the centrally located guesthouse of the University of Hamburg.

The guesthouse provides fully furnished apartments equipped with cooking facilities.

The institutions also welcome fellows accompanied by:

  • Life partners; and
  • Children.

HIAS and IFSH can provide assistance with finding:

  • Suitable accommodation;
  • Schools; and
  • Day care facilities.

This family-friendly approach can help researchers planning a stay of several months in Hamburg.

How Applications Will Be Evaluated

Applications are evaluated both on the applicant’s profile and the quality and suitability of the proposed research project.

Applicant Evaluation Criteria

Selection considers:

  1. A doctorate in the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, or life sciences;
  2. Publications in relevant academic journals or comparable publication outlets;
  3. Evidence of an interdisciplinary and international research profile;
  4. Research experience related to the fellowship’s core research areas;
  5. Prestigious prizes and awards, where relevant; and
  6. A very good command of English.

Career stage will also be considered, with particular attention given to the future potential of early-career researchers.

Project Evaluation Criteria

Reviewers will consider whether the proposed project:

  1. Opens up new questions and ways of thinking;
  2. Benefits from interaction with other academic disciplines;
  3. Addresses questions connected to the fellowship’s core research topics;
  4. Is suitable for an Institute for Advanced Study environment;
  5. Can be matched with an appropriate IFSH tandem partner; and
  6. Is feasible within the research environments of HIAS, IFSH, and Hamburg.

Applicants should therefore make a clear case not only for the quality of their research idea but also for why Hamburg, HIAS, and IFSH are appropriate environments for undertaking the project.

Application Requirements

Applications must be submitted in English.

All required documents should be combined and uploaded as one PDF file through the official application form.

Applicants should prepare the following materials carefully.

1. Cover Letter

The cover letter should state:

  • The applicant’s desired fellowship period;
  • Possible academic tandem partner or partners at IFSH;
  • Any possible partial financing through a sabbatical, paid leave, or similar arrangement, where applicable; and
  • How the applicant’s research profile would enrich the fellowship group, IFSH, and the wider Hamburg research environment.

The cover letter provides candidates with an opportunity to explain why they are particularly well suited to the fellowship and how their participation could contribute to the broader intellectual community.

2. Letter of Intent From a Prospective Tandem Partner

Applicants may include a one-page letter of intent from their prospective IFSH tandem partner where applicable.

Importantly, this document is not mandatory for every applicant.

A letter of intent is requested only where the applicant and prospective tandem partner:

  • Are already acquainted; and
  • Intend to collaborate.

Applicants who have not previously contacted an IFSH researcher can simply name a possible tandem partner in their application.

Prior contact is therefore not required.

3. List of Most Important Publications

Applicants should provide a list of their most important publications.

The publication list must not exceed two pages.

Candidates should use this section to demonstrate the relevance and strength of their research record.

4. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a CV.

The CV should include relevant professional and academic information as well as details of:

  • Prizes; and
  • Awards.

Applicants should ensure that the CV clearly demonstrates their academic trajectory, relevant research experience, and interdisciplinary or international experience.

5. Research Project Description

Applicants must provide a description of their planned fellowship project.

The project description must not exceed three pages.

Given the evaluation criteria, applicants should clearly explain:

  • The research problem or question;
  • The project’s relevance;
  • Its innovative contribution;
  • Its relationship to the fellowship’s research priorities;
  • Its interdisciplinary dimensions;
  • Why interaction with other disciplines would benefit the project;
  • Why HIAS and IFSH provide an appropriate research environment; and
  • How the project can realistically be completed or substantially advanced during the proposed fellowship period.

6. Project Description for a Non-Specialist Audience

Applicants must also submit a separate description of their project aimed at a non-specialist audience.

This document must not exceed one page.

This requirement reflects the fellowship’s interest in projects that can contribute to broader public understanding.

Applicants should therefore communicate the significance and objectives of their research in clear and accessible language.

7. Optional Online Video, Talk or Lecture

Applicants may additionally provide a link to an online:

  • Video;
  • Talk; or
  • Lecture.

This component is optional.

Application Deadline

The deadline to submit an application for the HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program is:

November 16, 2026

Applications must be uploaded in English as a single PDF file through the official application form by the deadline.

Prospective applicants should allow sufficient time to prepare their research proposal, publication list, CV, cover letter, and non-specialist project description.

Data Processing

Applicants should be aware that submitting an application constitutes consent to the purpose-related processing of their personal data.

Application information will be shared with:

  • HIAS committees;
  • IFSH committees; and
  • External reviewers where necessary.

Applicants should take this into account when submitting their application materials.

Application Enquiries

Applicants with questions regarding the application procedure or required documents may contact:

Dr. Kerstin Bischl
Email: bischl@ifsh.de

Candidates are encouraged to carefully review the requirements and prepare all required documents before submitting their application.

APPLY NOW

Why Consider the HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program?

The fellowship offers researchers the opportunity to combine independent scholarship with interdisciplinary engagement in one of Germany’s major academic cities.

Among its key features are:

  • A funded research stay in Hamburg, Germany;
  • Fellowship periods ranging from three to nine months;
  • Freedom to pursue an independent research project;
  • A stipend or reimbursement arrangement through IFSH;
  • A fully equipped workspace in central Hamburg;
  • Collaboration with an academic tandem partner at IFSH;
  • Access to relevant local research networks and infrastructure;
  • Opportunities to connect with researchers across HIAS member institutions;
  • Participation in an interdisciplinary international fellowship community;
  • Weekly academic lunches, colloquia, and dinners;
  • Opportunities for additional excursions;
  • Potential accommodation in the University of Hamburg guesthouse;
  • Support for fellows relocating with partners and children; and
  • Assistance with accommodation, schools, and day care.

The program is particularly relevant for researchers whose work engages with contemporary questions of peace, security, political violence, European security, international strategic competition, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, climate change, disaster preparedness, resilience, and civil protection.

Important Dates at a Glance

Prospective applicants should keep the following dates and conditions in mind:

  • Application deadline: November 16, 2026
  • Earliest fellowship start: October 2027
  • Normal academic year: October 1 to June 30
  • Minimum fellowship duration: Three months
  • Maximum fellowship duration: Nine months
  • Non-fellowship months: July, August, and September
  • Location: Hamburg, Germany
  • Working arrangement: On-site at HIAS and IFSH

Conclusion

The HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program 2027 in Germany provides an important opportunity for accomplished scholars to pursue independent and interdisciplinary research on some of the most significant peace and security challenges facing societies today.

With research areas spanning political violence, polarisation, radicalisation, counterterrorism, great power competition, deterrence, cybersecurity, European security, climate change, disaster preparedness, crisis resilience, and civil protection, the program offers considerable scope for researchers working across the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and life sciences.

Beyond providing time for independent research, the fellowship places significant emphasis on intellectual exchange. Fellows become part of the academic communities of HIAS and IFSH, work alongside an IFSH tandem partner, connect with researchers across Hamburg, and participate actively in an interdisciplinary academic program.

The availability of fellowship funding, a fully equipped workspace, institutional assistance, potential guesthouse accommodation, and support for accompanying partners and children also makes the program suitable for scholars seeking an extended research stay in Germany.

Qualified researchers interested in joining the program should begin preparing their application documents well ahead of the November 16, 2026 deadline, ensuring that their proposed project clearly demonstrates originality, interdisciplinary potential, relevance to the fellowship’s research priorities, and suitability for the HIAS and IFSH research environment in Hamburg.

item.content:encoded:
CorpsAfrica is accepting applications for its Development Associate position in Washington, DC, offering an opportunity for early-career professionals interested in fundraising, donor relations, nonprofit management, communications, community development, and international development.

The full-time position offers an annual salary of $55,000 to $60,000 and is designed for a professional who can combine strong communication and relationship-building abilities with careful donor data management, prospect research, event support, and cross-departmental collaboration.

The Development Associate will work closely with CorpsAfrica’s Donor Relations Manager and contribute to efforts to expand and strengthen the organisation’s donor base. The successful candidate will support donor cultivation and stewardship, fundraising campaigns, donor events, prospect research, financial reconciliation, and the maintenance of accurate donor information.

The position is based in Washington, DC, with a hybrid arrangement requiring two days per week, although remote work may also be considered. The successful applicant should also be willing to travel domestically and internationally for up to 20% of their time.

Applications must be submitted by September 30, 2026.

About CorpsAfrica

CorpsAfrica is an organisation focused on empowering young Africans to lead community-driven development initiatives within their own countries and across the African continent.

The organisation was founded in 2011 by former Peace Corps Volunteer Liz Fanning. The idea behind CorpsAfrica emerged from her experience with young Moroccans who expressed an interest in becoming Peace Corps Volunteers so they could contribute to communities in their own country.

At the time, the Peace Corps opportunity was available to Americans serving internationally. CorpsAfrica was subsequently developed around a different model: creating opportunities for young Africans to serve as volunteers and contribute to locally led development across Africa.

CorpsAfrica launched its first programme in Morocco in 2013. Since then, the organisation has expanded significantly across the continent.

According to CorpsAfrica, its programmes have operated across countries including:

  • Morocco
  • Senegal
  • Malawi
  • Rwanda
  • Kenya
  • South Africa
  • The Gambia
  • Ghana
  • Côte d’Ivoire
  • Ethiopia

The organisation has expanded to 11 countries and has an ambitious long-term objective of eventually reaching all 54 African countries.

Hundreds of CorpsAfrica Volunteers have participated in the organisation’s programmes, supporting more than 800 community projects.

These projects have covered a broad range of community priorities, including:

  • Building wells
  • Constructing schools
  • Developing roads
  • Establishing irrigation systems
  • Creating literacy programmes
  • Supporting vegetable farming
  • Supporting livestock farming
  • Advancing community-led development initiatives

The organisation’s broader approach centres on enabling communities and local changemakers to identify priorities and participate actively in designing and implementing solutions.

About the CorpsAfrica Development Associate Position

The Development Associate will support CorpsAfrica as the organisation continues to develop its donor community and strengthen its culture of philanthropy.

Rather than concentrating exclusively on fundraising outreach, the position combines donor-facing relationship management with operational fundraising responsibilities.

The successful candidate will work closely with the Donor Relations Manager to cultivate, steward, and strengthen relationships with donors.

An important part of the position involves ensuring donors receive timely and professional communication while maintaining accurate records of their engagement with CorpsAfrica.

The Development Associate will also help identify and qualify potential donors, support donor relations strategies, assist with fundraising events and campaigns, and track and analyse donor activity.

This means candidates should be comfortable moving between communication-oriented responsibilities and detailed administrative and data-management work.

Position Details

Key information about the vacancy includes:

  • Position: Development Associate
  • Organisation: CorpsAfrica
  • Location: Washington, DC
  • Employment type: Full-time
  • Classification: Exempt
  • Experience level: Entry level
  • Salary: $55,000–$60,000 annually
  • Working arrangement: Hybrid, two days per week, with remote work considered
  • Reports to: Donor Relations Manager
  • Travel: Domestic and international travel of up to 20%
  • Application deadline: September 30, 2026

Key Responsibilities of the Development Associate

The Development Associate will have responsibilities spanning donor stewardship, database management, fundraising operations, prospect research, events, communications, and financial coordination.

1. Donor Acknowledgements and Stewardship

One of the central responsibilities of the position is supporting positive and professional relationships between CorpsAfrica and its donors.

The Development Associate will be responsible for processing donor receipts and acknowledgements promptly.

Timely donor acknowledgement is an important component of nonprofit fundraising because it ensures supporters receive appropriate recognition for their contributions while helping the organisation maintain strong relationships with its donor community.

The Associate will also help maintain high-quality donor information within Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud.

2. Donor Data Management

Accurate data management will be another important component of the position.

The Development Associate will:

  • Enter donor information into relevant systems
  • Update existing donor records
  • Verify donor information
  • Maintain accurate fundraising data
  • Support reporting requirements
  • Help ensure fundraising records remain organised and reliable

The role will support both fundraising and finance teams, making attention to detail particularly important.

Candidates with experience using donor databases or customer relationship management systems may therefore have relevant experience for this position.

3. Cross-Departmental Collaboration

The Development Associate will not work exclusively within one team.
